questions.worked_solution:

$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following numbers lie in the fourth quadrant in an Argand diagram?

- $3+4\text{i}$
- $-2+3\text{i}$
- $1-2\text{i}$
questions.worked_solution:
- The complex number $3+4\text{i}$ has the real part $x=3$ and the imaginary part $y=4.$ So, it corresponds to the point $(3,4)$, which lies in the first quadrant.

- The complex number $-2+3\text{i}$ has the real part $x=-2$ and the imaginary part $y=3.$ So, it corresponds to the point $(-2,3)$, which lies in the second quadrant.

- The complex number $1-2\text{i}$ has the real part $x=1$ and the imaginary part $y=-2.$ So, it corresponds to the point $(1,-2)$, which lies in the fourth quadrant.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035975/assets/a4f87e680d46b099b9543b552191c776ac7145fba4e1b51b10c44a3685907d46.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".

questions.worked_solution:

- The complex number $-2+\text{i}$ has the real part $x=-2$ and the imaginary part $y=1.$ So, it corresponds to the point $(-2,1)$, which lies in the second quadrant.

- The complex number $-1+2\text{i}$ has the real part $x=-1$ and the imaginary part $y=2.$ So, it corresponds to the point $(-1,2)$, which lies in the second quadrant.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035975/assets/9f2e7234ba52d14098e0ecfc9695181b425764c110995b76b4b0efddf206252c.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only".

questions.problem:
Which of the following numbers lie in the fourth quadrant in an Argand diagram?

- $\frac{3}{2}-\text{i}$
- $-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\text{i}$
- $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{2}\text{i}$
questions.worked_solution:
- The complex number $\frac{3}{2}-\text{i}$ has the real part $x=\frac{3}{2}$ and the imaginary part $y=-1.$ So, it corresponds to the point $(\frac{3}{2},-1)$, which lies in the fourth quadrant.

- The complex number $-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\text{i}$ has the real part $x=-\frac{1}{2}$ and the imaginary part $y=-\frac{1}{2}.$ So, it corresponds to the point $(-\frac{1}{2},-\frac{1}{2})$, which lies in the third quadrant.

- The complex number $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{2}\text{i}$ has the real part $x=\frac{1}{2}$ and the imaginary part $y=\frac{3}{2}.$ So, it corresponds to the point $(\frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{2})$, which lies in the first quadrant.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035975/assets/d7390ddcc8d338d2fd46bc12b0a4c65f8e6bf6e8c4f6c9fa802e2acea159416b.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".
